test_title: PYST 13: SSC GD Constable - Quantitative Aptitude (Held on: 30th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: In a family 5 people spend 10% on the purchase of sugar. The price of sugar increased by 10%. What should be the percentage decrease in the consumption of sugar so as not to increase the expenditure?
solution:
**Given:**

The price of sugar is increased by 10%

**Formula used:**

Expenditure = Price × Quantity

Percentage reduction in a Quantity = (Old quantity - New quantity)/Old quantity × 100

**Calculation:**

If Price is increased in ratio a : b

Then, to keep the expenditure same 

The quantity should be reduced in the ratio b : a

Here, price is increaseby 10% 

Ratio of price change = 10 : 11

⇒ Ratio of quantity = 11 : 10

Reduction in quantity = (11 - 10)/11 = 1/11

Percent reduction in quantity = 1/11 × 100 = 9(1)/(11)%

**∴ Percentage decrease in the consumption of sugar so as to not increase the expenditure is 9(1)/(11)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** Let the price of sugar be 100

Increase price of sugar = 100 × 1.1 = 110 (∵ 10% increase)

Let the initial quantity of sugar purchased = 10

Old expenditure on sugar = 100 × 10 = 1000

New expenditure = Increased price × New quantity

Keeping the expenditure same

⇒ 1000 = 110 × New quantity

⇒ New quantity = 100/11

Percentage Reduction in quantity = (10 - 100/11)/10 × 100 

⇒ (110 - 100)/110 × 100

⇒ 1/11 × 100

⇒ 9(1)/(11)%

∴ Percentage decrease in consumption is 9(1)/(11)%.
